Subject: Draft MAP & evaluation timeline for Skyline POC

Hi Alyssa / Tom,

Thanks again for the call today — great alignment on the success criteria for the POC. Attached is a draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and an initial evaluation schedule keyed to your internal stakeholders. Key dates:

- MAP kickoff: 2026-05-10
- Technical evaluation (runbook / 1-week): 2026-05-17 to 2026-05-23
- Business validation / exec review: week of 2026-05-24
- Target close (contracts signed): 2026-06-01

Please review the MAP and the evaluation plan (attached). If procurement or security needs additional artifacts, we can push those into the evaluation week.

Next steps:
- Alyssa: confirm decision-maker availability for the week of 5/24
- Tom: share any outstanding security questions so we can prep answers before the technical kickoff
- We: finalize MAP v2 and circulate by Monday (5/4)

Attachments: skyline_map_v2.xlsx, eval_plan_v1.pdf

Best,

Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700

Connor — thanks for the plan and the attachments. We're excited, but a quick heads-up: procurement just told me their earliest they can sign off on the SOW is mid-May (they're tied up with a vendor RFP). That means the technical resources we planned for 5/17 may not be available until ~5/31.

Two asks:
1) Can you push the technical evaluation two weeks later and share an updated MAP?
2) If we need temporary access for a smaller sandbox earlier, can you propose a short scoped evaluation that won't need procurement sign-off?

I'll follow up with procurement and keep you posted.

—Alyssa

Head of Product, Skyline Health
alyssa@skyline.tech
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 08:26:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Procurement delay from Skyline — suggested triage

Folks — forwarding Alyssa's note. Procurement slip looks like it will push our technical window ~2 weeks. Quick read on impact and recommended next steps below.

Impact assessment (quick):
- Revenue close likely slides from 2026-06-01 to ~2026-06-15 if nothing else changes.
- Risk: competitive re-bid risk increases (they're running an RFP).
- Technical/QA: our preferred evaluator block shifts and may conflict with other POCs in that week.

Suggested mitigation options:
1) Re-baseline MAP dates to preserve the deal but accept a 2-week close slip.
2) Offer a limited sandbox pilot (no contract) to keep momentum and let product teams test earlier.
3) Small commercial concession (30-day credit / pilot discount) if procurement insists on late start and to reduce re-bid risk.

I can own the messaging to Alyssa proposing options 1+2; if we want to offer option 3 I need a quick sign-off (Marissa/Laura).

Also attached a quick risk register stub I'm starting (risk_register.csv) — will populate once we decide route.

Connor
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: connor_obrien <connor@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 6 May 2026 10:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Procurement delay from Skyline — suggested triage

Thanks Connor — noted. I recommend we do a two-track approach:

- Primary: re-baseline the MAP and formally shift technical evaluation to 5/31–6/06 and close target to 6/15. Update the MAP doc and send a clean calendar with the new blocks.
- Secondary (momentum play): offer a non-contract sandbox (1-week, limited tokens, sample data only) that Alyssa's team can use immediately to validate integration. This doesn't require procurement sign-off.

On commercial concessions: I'm okay to approve a one-time 30-day credit (to be applied post-close) if it meaningfully reduces re-bid risk. Cost impact is minimal compared to the ACV. Rafael should be looped for visibility/approval.

I'll update the risk_register.csv and attach a short summary. Attaching: risk_register.csv, skyline_map_v2.xlsx (with new dates).

Marissa Cole
Director, Sales Operations
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 8 May 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Escalation: approval request — Skyline concession (30-day credit)

Hi Rafael — quick note: Skyline (RDW-2319) is at moderate risk of slipping out of our quarter due to procurement timing and a competing RFP. Marissa and Connor suggest a one-time 30-day credit as a mitigation to keep them engaged and reduce re-bid probability.

Why this helps:
- Low short-term cost; preserves ACV and customer relationship.
- Gives us leverage to lock technical evaluation dates and an agreed close target (we'll move to 6/15).

Request: please approve the 30-day credit (applied at invoice) and confirm if legal needs to add a small amendment. If approved, Connor will send updated MAP + concession language to Alyssa this week.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
VP, Sales — Enterprise Accounts
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@skyline.tech>

Subject: Re: Draft MAP & evaluation timeline for Skyline POC — timeline update

Alyssa — thanks for the update and for flagging procurement. Per our internal triage, we can do both: re-baseline and a short sandbox to keep momentum. 

What we're proposing now:
- Re-baselined technical evaluation: 2026-05-31 to 2026-06-06
- Re-baselined close target: 2026-06-15
- Immediate temporary sandbox: 7-day scoped sandbox (limited tokens, does not require SOW) — accessible by next business day once you confirm a list of < 5 testers
- Commercial concession: one-time 30-day credit post-close (we'll add a short amendment if legal needs it)

I've attached the updated MAP (skyline_map_v2.xlsx) and a short evaluation playbook for the sandbox (eval_plan_v1.pdf). If that sounds good, can you confirm: (1) sandbox tester list and (2) approval to move technical eval to 5/31?

We'll hold the 5/17 date on our side for internal planning but will not run the block unless you confirm earlier availability.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
